units.summary: New test. It evicts a non-stale series through CompactSelectedSeries, forces a WAL checkpoint with mint 150 (below the recorded walExpiry of 200), and asserts that the series record is still in the checkpoint. It is test-only and mirrors the existing CompactStaleHead test.
units.headline: Test: selected-series eviction keeps series record in WAL checkpoint
units.reason: A new test that only adds coverage and cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: gcStaleSeries is renamed to gcSeries and now takes a shouldEvict predicate. numStaleSeries now drops only by the number of evicted series that actually ended in a stale-NaN, where it used to drop by every removed series. This keeps the stale gauge correct now that non-stale series can be evicted through CompactSelectedSeries.
units.headline: gcSeries takes eviction predicate; stale counter counts only stale deletions
units.reason: Changes the eviction decision and the head stale-series accounting, which other code relies on.
focus: numStaleSeries is now decremented by staleSeriesDeleted rather than len(deleted); check this matches how the counter is incremented on append
walExpiries are still set for every deleted ref, whatever the predicate decided

units.summary: The hard-coded stale-NaN check is replaced by the caller's shouldEvict predicate, which runs under the series lock after the maxTime check. The function also counts how many deleted series were stale, using the same isStaleSeries logic as the regular head gc. The CompactStaleHead caller keeps its stale check inside its predicate, so its behavior is unchanged.
units.headline: Stripe gcSeries uses caller predicate instead of hard-coded stale check
units.reason: Generalises which series get deleted from the head, so a wrong predicate or call path could silently drop series.
focus: shouldEvict runs with series.Lock held; hasAppendIDAbove requires that lock
isStaleSeries is evaluated before deletion under the lock, matching the gc() stale count logic
